newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea physical crude buying shrinks June overhang.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea physical crude buying shrinks June overhang.

text.p: North Sea physical crudes traded at steady to easier levels in active business on Wednesday, chipping away at the overhang of June barrels that continues to pressure values, traders said.
"It's been a day for buying," a senior North Sea crude trader said, noting up to 10 cargoes had moved. "It's been a mix of end-user buying and people looking at possible storage."
Wednesday's activity meant that around 12 non-Brent June cargoes remained on the market. Dealers hope the steep price contango will push barrels into storage and relieve the overhang of June barrels.
A cargo of Brent loading June 17-19 changed hands at July Brent -70 cents, unchanged from Tuesday when a cargo loading the same dates moved also at a 70 cent discount.
A late rumour that a second Brent cargo was traded was denied by the European major said to be involved.
Other trades included a June 25-27 Draugen at Dated +10 cents and a June 27-29 Ekofisk sold weaker at Dated -1 cent.
About five Statfjords moved and while the values were not disclosed traders said they appeared to be in the range of Dated Brent -5 cents/+5 cents, unchanged to slightly weaker.
One trader said he had heard three of the Statfjord values at were Dated -1 cent, Dated evens and Dated +5 cents.
An Ekofisk loading July 1-3 changed hands at Dated -3 cents.
Outright prices were steady to slightly firmer on Wednesday, after seven straight sessions of losses, helped by news of Iraqi interference with United Nations' helicopters.
London July futures for benchmark Brent Blend crude oil gained five cents to $17.55 a barrel by 1756 GMT after dipping as low as $17.45 on Tuesday, a level not seen since May 1996.
Most players saw the API stock data as broadly neutral.
Market talk earlier was balanced between those expecting weaker differentials and those thinking Brent had hit bottom.
The only Brent cargo nominated loading dates of June 26-28 was kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline. Traders said the cargo was kept by Glencore.
The July/August intermonth was three cents stronger at -27/-26 cents and August/September was two to three cents higher at -21/-19 cents.
Next week's contracts for difference were slightly perkier at August Brent -68/-61 cents, with the folliowing week at August Brent -55/-50 cents.
